chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the sick person when he is unable to stand and prostrate. He said: 'He can gesture with his head, and for him to place his forehead on the ground is more beloved to me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a sick person who cannot stand or prostrate during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of physical exertion in prayer, establishing that while head nodding (iima') is legally sufficient for those unable to prostrate, placing the forehead directly on the ground is preferred (afdal) as it more closely mimics the complete ruku' and sujud. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing ease (rukhas) with the preservation of the prayer's essential form, ensuring the sick person maintains the dignity of worship without undue hardship.
